_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
Tuesday March 17 | 5:45 a.m

Bonjour Tremblant!

Today brings another day of significant and variable weather conditions, including high winds. Overnight, temperatures remained mild, but they are now beginning to drop. This morning, we’re seeing beautiful snowfall with large flakes, with 7 cm of fresh snow already on the ground, and conditions will continue to get colder throughout the day. Our mountain crews are working hard to prepare the terrain and provide the best possible skiing and snowboarding conditions. Runs will open progressively as they are safely ready. We’re committed to making your day on the mountain as enjoyable as possible. We encourage everyone to come prepared for changing weather and variable conditions.
Please check this page regularly for important updates throughout the day.

First Tracks
Access to designated lifts, on both North and South side, as early as 7:45 a.m.
Ski on designated North Side slopes at 8 a.m.

It’s Ontario spring break, and we’re excited to welcome so many skiers and snowboarders to the mountain. Be sure to join us at Place St-Bernard for activities from 2:30 to 9:00 p.m

Enjoy your time on the mountain!

Mountain safety tip of the week: Après-ski is after skiing!
Do NOT use ski lifts or ski runs if you are under the influence of drugs or alcohol.
This is required under the Mountain Code of Conduct.
Stay Sharp on the Slopes
  • Collisions and falls increase when your concentration, awareness, and reaction time are reduced.
  • Drugs and alcohol impair your abilities on the slopes just like they do on the road.
  • Protect yourself and others—ski responsibly.
Snow fall is recorded daily at 5 a.m from mid-mountain at North Side (550 m / 1,800 ft). This data, based on 24 hours, provides a picture of on-mountain conditions. Actual accumulation may differ from the official report. Be aware of changing conditions. Lifts and trails exist in a mountain environment and may close due to weather, usage and/or special maintenance.
